`v0.9.0.db` was written by weft **v0.9.0** (the tag, from the module proxy) through `otel.Local(path)` with a `wefttest.Script` model: one run, `r_v090`, agent `orders`, two steps (a `lookup_order` tool call, then the answer). Tests copy it before opening — Studio migrates a file it opens.

To regenerate or audit it: put the program below at `examples/studio-local/internal/mkv090db/main.go` (that module pins `github.com/weftgo/weft v0.9.0`; `GOWORK=off` keeps the workspace from substituting the local tree), run from `examples/studio-local`

```sh
GOWORK=off GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run ./internal/mkv090db /path/to/v0.9.0.db
```

then delete the program (it is not committed). The committed file is exactly what the program wrote.

```go
// Throwaway: record one 2-step run with weft v0.9.0 into a fresh sqlite file.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/weftgo/weft"
	"github.com/weftgo/weft/otel"
	"github.com/weftgo/weft/wefttest"
)

type in struct {
	OrderID string `json:"order_id" jsonschema:"the order"`
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	path := os.Args[1]
	p, err := otel.Start(ctx, otel.Local(path), otel.NoGlobal())
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	lookup := weft.Tool("lookup_order", "Look up an order.", func(context.Context, in) (string, error) {
		return "order 42 shipped", nil
	})
	agent := weft.New(wefttest.Script(
		wefttest.ToolCalls(wefttest.Call{Name: "lookup_order", Args: `{"order_id":"42"}`, ID: "c1"}),
		wefttest.Say("Order 42 shipped this morning."),
	), weft.Name("orders"), weft.Instructions("You are a support agent."), lookup,
		weft.TracerProvider(p.TracerProvider()), weft.LoggerProvider(p.LoggerProvider()))
	if _, err := agent.Generate(ctx, weft.RunID("r_v090"), weft.Prompt("Where is order 42?")); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := p.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```
